stem: A clinical research study measures treatment response rate across 5 trial sites, each containing multiple patient cohorts. trial site A has 5 observations with mean 54.4 % (within-trial site SD = 9.4). trial site B has 10 observations with mean 52.8 % (within-trial site SD = 7.5). trial site C has 20 observations with mean 66.9 % (within-trial site SD = 7.8). trial site D has 10 observations with mean 56.2 % (within-trial site SD = 7.5). trial site E has 5 observations with mean 59.8 % (within-trial site SD = 7.1). The between-trial site standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 4.4 and 11.1 %. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true treatment response rate for trial site A, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-trial site variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for trial site A: 55.8 % (shrunk from raw 54.4). Range [55.1, 57.1] as between-trial site SD varies from 4.4 to 11.1. Pooled mean: 60.0.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 60.0 % (weighted average of 5 trial site means).
Shrinkage factor for trial site A: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/5). At σ_between=7.4: B = 0.756.
Interval [55.1, 57.1] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (54.4) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (60.0) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
